decisions.reason: As a newly introduced but strategically important particle-therapy QA device with unresolved market uncertainty and a recent release delay rather than clear failure, it is more valuable as an option to keep than to abandon now.
This small-volume ionization chamber fits the firm's core dosimetry portfolio, likely costs little to keep available, and has had too little time on the market to justify withdrawal.
Although it may overlap somewhat with other chamber offerings, it still represents a low-cost real option in a core measurement category and there is not yet enough evidence to drop it.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models is closely aligned with routine customer needs and the firm's established capabilities, making early withdrawal unlikely.
The product is a specialized but coherent extension of the firm's radiation-measurement offering, so management would likely keep it on the market while demand uncertainty resolves.
Despite some possible overlap with other ionization chambers, a thimble chamber is a familiar category in the firm's core business and is worth retaining as a relatively inexpensive option.
